issues.failure_explanation: Applying the displayed polarization identity to (1/θ)(v_θ, v_θ−v^n) gives a dissipation term (θ−1/2)|v^{n+1}−v^n|^2, not (θ−1/2)/2 |v^{n+1}−v^n|^2. The same factor error appears for the potential-gradient term. Thus the stated energy balance has half the correct dissipation coefficient. The fully discrete Proposition repeats the same erroneous factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the extra 1/2 in the dissipation term, using (θ−1/2)[ρ|δv|^2 + α^{-1}|∇δφ|^2] (and the corresponding discrete sum) instead of (θ−1/2)/2 times that quantity.
issues.overall_effect: The exact energy-balance equalities in the semi-discrete Lemma and the fully discrete Proposition are false as written. The energy stability inequality for θ≥1/2 still has the correct sign, but the claimed exact balance is incorrect.
issues.title: Energy balance dissipation term is too small by a factor of two
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local algebraic factor error; correcting the coefficient restores the exact balance and preserves the intended stability result.

issues.failure_explanation: The bilinear form depends only on gradients. Any nonzero constant φ has ∇φ=0, so a(φ,φ)=0. Hence it is not coercive on all of H^1(domain). Coercivity requires either H^1_0(domain), a zero-mean subspace, or explicit boundary conditions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the space as H^1_0(domain) or H^1(domain)/R (or assume homogeneous Dirichlet/zero-mean boundary conditions).
issues.overall_effect: The stated well-posedness of the Poisson-like problem is not established for the space H^1(domain) as written; boundary conditions or a quotient/zero-mean condition are missing.
issues.title: Coercivity claimed on full H^1 without boundary or zero-mean condition
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard boundary or zero-mean condition is a local fix and does not change the intended method or conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: For φ_h∈H_h, ∇φ_h need not belong to V_h^d on non-affine meshes. The lumped inner product is defined only for functions in V_h (or V_h^d), so the term ⟨ρ B^{-1}∇φ_h, ∇ψ_h⟩_h is not defined by the given definition. The scheme is therefore ill-defined as written on the advertised non-affine meshes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the lumped inner product to piecewise continuous functions (or to gradients by nodal evaluation), or restrict the mesh assumption to affine meshes.
issues.overall_effect: The fully discrete bilinear form, well-posedness, and energy balance are not well-defined on non-affine meshes unless the inner product is extended to gradients or affine meshes are assumed.
issues.title: Lumped inner product applied to gradients not in V_h on non-affine meshes
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local definitional extension that preserves the intended scheme and does not require a new global argument.

issues.failure_explanation: If δE^{n+1} > E_kin^{n+1}, then 1 − max(0, δE/E_kin) = 1 − δE/E_kin < 0, so the square root is not real. The relaxation step is therefore not well-defined in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a capped expression such as sqrt(max(0, 1 − δE/E_kin)) or set the kinetic energy to zero when δE exceeds E_kin.
issues.overall_effect: The restart-with-relaxation procedure can fail to produce a real momentum update, so the claimed energy-balance repair is not guaranteed.
issues.title: Gauss law restart relaxation can take square root of a negative number
issues.why_classification: A local cap or max fixes well-definedness without changing the intended relaxation strategy.
